newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia proposes tax incentives for Labuan.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia proposes tax incentives for Labuan.

text.p: Malaysia has proposed a income tax exemption of 50 percent on certain foreign workers serving in offshore companies in the Labuan offshore financial centre, Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim said in his 1997 Budget speech on Friday.
The exemption applies to gross income of foreign workers at the managerial level serving in offshore companies, which will be extended up to the year of assessment in 2000, Anwar said.

Income from qualifying professional services such as financial, accounting, secretarial and legal services provided to offshore companies is exempted from income tax up to 50 percent of the adjusted income of that source, Anwar said.
He said the incentive is given up to the year of assessment 1997.
In addition, Malaysia is proposing no withholding tax on royalty, interest and technical fee paid by offshore companies to non-residents.
The measures are meant to to promote Labuan as a competitive offshore financial centre to rival other tax-free havens.
